course_description:
This course provides you with the opportunity to critically evaluate published clinical research and reflect on your own clinical practice. Through guided research activities, you will explore topics of personal and clinical relevance. The course is intentionally flexible, allowing you to tailor your research to align with your individual clinical interests and experience.

As a core component of the Master of Medicine (Skin Cancer) program, this course highlights the importance of evidence-based decision-making. We hope you will find that, as you progress through this course, these essential principles are foundational to delivering quality patient care and add intellectual stimulation to your daily clinical practice. Whether interpreting literature to address clinical questions or undertaking original research, the ability to apply these principles is fundamental to skin cancer medicine.

learning_outcomes.description: Apply principles of audit and research methodology to analyse clinical practice in skin cancer management.
Identify gaps in practice and generate innovative, evidence-informed strategies for quality improvement.
Disseminate audit findings to contribute to healthcare system improvement.
Embed equity and inclusion in research design and quality improvement projects.
Communicate research and audit outcomes clearly to academic, professional, and clinical audiences.
Uphold ethical standards in research and promote leadership in quality improvement initiatives.

assessment_summary.title: Critical appraisal of a scientific paper - Report

assessment_details.title: Critical appraisal of a scientific paper - Report
assessment_details.task_description: You should choose and review a journal article from the list provided.You will assess the scientific quality of the article and write a critique of the key features of the manuscript. The report should critically evaluate key aspects such as the clarity and relevance of study aims, the suitability of the study design, the quality of the background and discussion and study limitations. The report will additionally discuss the clinical relevance of the paper's content to your area of work in clinical skin cancer medicine. Expected word count is maximum 2000 words. assessment_details.title: Surgical Database Audit Report
assessment_details.task_description: You will be required to submit a clinical log via use of the SCARD database (or other appropriate clinical database). The log requires a minimum of 50 cases. Proper collation and entry of data will make analysis easier. You will complete an audit of your own patients, including a written analysis (2000 words) comparing your results with those from the broader SCARD database (or other database) of skin cancer practitioners The Introduction/rationale must include a description of your clinical practice. Although a detailed knowledge of statistics is not required, it is expected some basic analytical principles be employed when looking at the data. Analysis of raw data will be complete when accompanied by literature research, contemplation of how these results tabulate with your patient population and medical practice setup. assessment_details.title: Literature Review
assessment_details.task_description: Clinical practice is built on a foundation of published knowledge. Reviewing published work is an essential part of professional development. The final assessment is the preparation of a literature review (maximum 2500 words) in an area relevant to skin cancer. You will select a topic from the list provided. You are to write a structured literature review using the framework provided. Details will be made available on the course Learn.UQ site. At the end of this course, students completing this task should be confident in preparing a journal article and to feel comfortable with the concept of possibly publishing future work.
